b.answer:
Worked example: Bright Path Academy, a fictional private school in Abeokuta that enrols pupils and sells after-school clubs.

Contact (parent) ──(parent of)── Contact (pupil, record only)
Deal (Enrolment) ── Company: none (families, not businesses)
Custom object: none needed. "Class" is a deal property (dropdown).
Ticket: fee queries and complaints

Pipelines

  • Enrolment: Enquiry → Tour booked → Toured → Assessment → Offer sent → Enrolled / Lost.
  • Clubs: same stages? No: Enquiry → Registered → Paid. Different process → separate pipeline.
  • Tickets: New → Bursar reviewing → Resolved.

Why no custom object: a class is just a label for reports, not a thing with its own records and links, so a dropdown on the deal is enough.
mistakes: Creating a custom object for something that is only a label.
Separate pipelines for things with the same stages (e.g. each campus).
b.pass: A diagram of objects and labelled associations, each pipeline with stages and exit rules, and a sentence justifying every custom object (or why none is needed).
b.redo: Send it back if a custom object isn't justified, two pipelines share the same stages, or service requests are modelled as sales.

s.answer:
Worked example: Bright Path Academy (fictional). Extract from the solution design.

object | label            | internal name      | type     | values / rule                 | required at
deal   | Class applied for| bpa_class          | dropdown | Nursery 1…JSS3                | create
deal   | Annual fee (NGN) | bpa_fee_ngn        | number   | > 0, whole naira              | Offer sent
deal   | Lost reason      | bpa_lost_reason    | dropdown | Fees · Distance · Chose other | Lost
contact| Lead source      | bpa_lead_source    | dropdown | Referral · Facebook · Walk-in | create
contact| Consent to mkt   | bpa_mkt_consent    | dropdown | yes · no · unknown + date     | create

Permission matrix: admissions officer (own deals, edit), bursar (all deals view, tickets edit, export none), principal and owner (all, export yes). Pupils' medical notes stay out of the CRM (kept in the school's records system).

Assignment: new enquiries to the admissions officer for the campus; deal name "Surname · Class · Year". Open questions with dates: whether to track siblings as a label (decision due 20 Nov).
mistakes: Data dictionary missing internal names or value lists.
Fields required at creation that can't be known yet.
Sensitive data (health, IDs) kept in the CRM without a reason.
s.pass: All eight design sections, a data dictionary with internal name, type, values and required stage for every custom field, and a least-privilege permission matrix within the plan's limits.
s.redo: Send it back if fields lack types or values, the design exceeds the plan's limits, or sensitive data is stored without justification.

g.answer:
Worked example of evidence (client name removed): a signed design v1.0 for a car dealership and a HubSpot trial configured from it.

  • Screenshots: Vehicle custom object (Enterprise trial) with 9 properties; Sales and Service pipelines; teams Lekki and Ikeja.
  • Test user "Sales rep (test)" sees only own deals; "Manager (test)" sees the team's; export disabled for both.
  • Change log: 3 differences between design and build, each resolved and dated.

Submit the design (redacted), the screenshots and the two-user permission test.
mistakes: Configuring before the design is signed.
Showing permissions only from the admin account.
Properties created that aren't in the dictionary.
No record of differences between design and build.
g.pass: A signed (or formally reviewed) design for a real client, the configuration in a trial or sandbox, and screenshots proving two roles see only what the matrix allows.
g.redo: Send it back if permissions are only asserted, not shown, or the configuration doesn't match the design.
